sources.title: Anode Materials for Lithium-Ion Batteries, from Conventional Materials to High-Entropy Oxides: A Review of Synthesis Methods, Properties and Sustainability Challenges

evidence.text_snippet: Lithium has been utilized as a pure metal in crafting anodes for Li-ion batteries since the 1970s. This material demonstrated its suitability for energy storage due to a significant characteristic—its high energy density, with lithium metal achieving an extraordinary theoretical specific capacity of 3861 mAhg−1 and 2062 mAhcm−3
As an alternative to metallic lithium, graphite has gained an important place in the batteries field, being a form of carbon with a layered structure.

morphology.description: nanowires, nanospheres, nanoparticles and silicon films

evidence.text_snippet: The theoretical capacity of Si is 3590 mAhg−1 resulting from the analysis of the fully alloyed form of Li 15Si4 at room temperature. This property increases to 4200 mAhg −1 at elevated temperatures and corresponds to the formation of Li 22Si5 compound.

One strategy focuses on creating hybrid nanostructured anodes, such as silicon nanoparticles attached to vertically aligned carbon nanotubes (VACNTs). This design accommodates silicon’s volume fluctuations, enhancing electrode stability and delivering a reversible capacity of 1330 mAh/g over 2000 cycles.
Another anode material used predominantly in the manufacture of Li-ion batteries is lithium titanate (Li4Ti5O12, LTO).
The compound Li4.4Sn, resulting from the alloying of pure tin with lithium, exhibits a high theoretical capacity (~944 mAh/g) compared to conventional graphite anodes
MWCNTs exhibit a discharge capacity of approximately 312 mAh/g. Chemical etching can further increase lithium storage capacities, with etched MWCNTs reaching values up to 2087 mAh/g

Graphene, represented as a monolayer of carbon atoms with sp2 bonds can offer remarkable properties as an anode material... This type of material provides a theoretical specific capacity of 744 mAh/g based on Li2C6

extraction_notes: This is a comprehensive review paper. In accordance with Rule 13, all extracted electrochemical performance data and specific material synthesis descriptions belong to cited prior literature summarized by the authors, rather than a focal primary experiment of this work.

OCR issue: Author names in the source contain raw OCR representation with commas instead of Romanian diacritics: e.g. 'S, erban' for Șerban, 'S, tefania' for Ștefania, 'Dragos, -Florin' for Dragoș-Florin, 'Ciurdas,' for Ciurdaș. Preserved exactly as printed in the PDF source text.
Table 2 contains a minor typo 'nMn2O4' which is explicitly known to be 'ZnMn2O4' in Section 3.3. Under rule 14, this has been preserved in the corresponding notes.
